This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `68c170d2256e995a69ad6eb85ef21a8aae451a4d` — the merge of head `7aeddce6f3626efe1fefaaa213b52685bea2ff24` into base `2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 68c170d2256e995a69ad6eb85ef21a8aae451a4d && git checkout 68c170d2256e995a69ad6eb85ef21a8aae451a4d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2 7aeddce6f3626efe1fefaaa213b52685bea2ff24 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2 && git merge --no-ff 7aeddce6f3626efe1fefaaa213b52685bea2ff24

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2
```

### ① Derived judgments

Face: narrowing — `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body's second line and in the changeset; no schema and no governed path in the diff (Governed Surface Queue Guard: success). 1. **Ruling 3C's first half — nothing stripped or refused: right.** The only behavioural edit is a `HoleEncoder` on the renderer's substitution pass (`template-renderer.ts` :43–59, :75–79). The html-face encoder is a five-character entity mapping, bijective on the value: every character survives, none is dropped, and no path returns a refusal. No write seam, validator, object definition or store is touched (`packages/spec`, `packages/objectql`, `packages/platform-objects`: untouched, as the claim requires). `plugin-email`'s pre-existing `htmlToText` / `stripTags` (`template-engine.ts` :214, :235) strips tags from a TEMPLATE body to derive a text part; it is not in the diff and reads no stored text field.
2. **The escaper covers the html contexts the claim names: right.** Ampersand, both angle brackets, the double quote and the single quote are mapped (:53–59) — the full set for element text and for an attribute value in either quote kind. It is the same mapping `plugin-email`'s engine already uses (`template-engine.ts` :89–95), so the two outlets now agree.
3. **Every hole form in an html or mjml body is escaped, none left raw, none added: right.** `renderNotification` has one hole grammar (`TOKEN`, :40 — a double-braced dotted path; the top-level conveniences `title`, `body`, `topic` and the spread payload keys resolve through the same `lookup`) and one body substitution (:128), which takes `escapeHtml` exactly when `format` is `html` or `mjml` (:127) and `verbatim` otherwise. No triple-brace or other raw arm exists in the grammar, before or after. The `format` vocabulary is the four-member select in `notification-template.object.ts` :159, so the two-way split is exhaustive.
4. **Subject, `markdown` and `text` bodies, and markup-free values are byte-identical to before: right.** `interpolate` is now `substitute(…, verbatim)` with `verbatim` the identity (:45, :71–73); `substitute`'s body is the former `interpolate` body with `encode(String(v))` in place of `String(v)` (:75–79), so the plain-text faces render the same bytes. The subject still goes through `interpolate` (:126). A value carrying none of the five characters passes `escapeHtml` unchanged, so an html or mjml body with markup-free values renders the same bytes too. The no-template fallback (:132–135) is untouched.
5. **The sender: right.** `email-channel.ts` :378–391 hands `rendered.subject` and `rendered.html` to the email service unchanged, so the mail's html part IS the renderer's html face. The channel's other arm (a notify step's `template`, :345) delegates to `plugin-email`'s `sendTemplate`, whose html face escapes by default (`email-service.ts` :1453–1457: `renderPlainTextTemplate` for subject and `body_text`, `renderTemplate` for `body_html`).
6. **The outlet census: right, with its radius stated.** Each pin file's list test asserts `touching` EQUALS `listed`, so a new shipped source that touches HTML — an identifier or string naming `html`, or a string carrying one of the enumerated element tags — turns the test red until classified, and a stale entry turns it red too; the control case proves comments never count. Ablation legs B, E and G in the PR body read 1/N red per package. The census's sight is stated in each file's LIMIT paragraph and holds: it reads this package only, by those two spellings, and proves nothing about a listed outlet's escaping (that is the per-entry pins' job). The per-package radius is the seat's ruling A (③). `translations/*.generated.ts` is excluded in `service-messaging` and `plugin-approvals` with a stated reason (a projection of the object declarations); `plugin-email`'s walker excludes nothing beyond tests and test kits.
7. **The per-entry pins drive the real render path: right.** `service-messaging`: `renderNotification` directly for html, mjml, subject, markdown and text; and `createEmailChannel` → the real store class subclassed to hand back one stored row → `renderNotification` → the structural `EmailSenderSurface` sink captured (the sink is the one double, and `check:engine-double-contract` is green on the head). `plugin-email`: the real `renderTemplate` / `renderPlainTextTemplate`; the real `EmailService` with a capture transport and a row loader; the built-ins pin iterates the real `BUILTIN_AUTH_TEMPLATES` bodies. One note, not a ground: `rowOf` re-maps a definition onto an `EmailTemplateRow` by hand (parallel to `template-loader.ts` :84) rather than through `createRegistryEmailTemplateLoader`; the bodies and the engine under test are real. `plugin-approvals`: the real `renderConfirmPage` / `renderResultPage` over `esc` (`action-link-pages.ts` :18).
8. **The built-ins' raw holes: right.** `auth-templates.ts` carries exactly 20 triple-braced holes in template bodies (a 21st textual match is the file's doc comment, which the pin never reads: it reads `bodyHtml`), every one inside a double-quoted `href` and naming a `type: 'url'` variable — the pin's two conditions. Ablation leg D read 10/66 red.
9. **The PR body's outlet table and the `sys_user.name` reading: consistent with the tree.** The census classifications match the code read. The `sys_user.name` reading cites the write validator's bounded-string branch, which exists (`record-validator.ts` :1082–1096, `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES`); the measurement itself was the dev's scratch run and is not re-run here (read-only).

Every skip is on `check-expected-skips.mjs`'s roster: the full-battery-only jobs (the Dogfood matrix placeholder, Dogfood Verify CLI, Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance), Build Docs (filter), the two opt-ins, and the `edited`-event runs of Auto Label and Check PR Size beside their concluded `opened` runs.

The claim amendment (6310385063) moved the arm; the PR body (line 2), the changeset and the bang title agree. One reading for the seat: what narrows is the rendered-output contract of one face (nothing accepted is refused), so the arm is the conservative one; it is not malformed, and it is the arm the dispatch's own trigger names.

The body bounds the contexts to element text and quoted attributes, and that bound is exactly what the escaper covers (①.2). FROM and TO are the before/after of :128.
